description: Static memento-vault benchmark task set for future Rondo clean evaluators and agent-development experiments.

issue.title: [P0] Create memento-vault benchmark task set for Rondo
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context
The Rondo/Beislið research recommends testing the externalized-knowledge/process theory against a small benchmark set of real memento-vault issues before claiming unattended reliability.

This benchmark data can be prepared now, even before Rondo runner changes land.

## Proposal
Create a memento-vault Rondo benchmark task set.

## Scope
Select 8-12 GitHub issues across categories:
- retrieval behavior
- MCP/tooling
- triage/capture
- docs/process
- sync/security/release

For each task, record:
- issue ID/title/body snapshot
- expected touched areas
- acceptance criteria
- required gates
- known risky areas
- relevant memento notes or docs to retrieve
- success/failure rubric

## Acceptance criteria
- Benchmark task definitions live in a machine-readable file or documented fixture directory.
- Tasks can be consumed later by Rondo or a clean evaluator.
- At least one task exercises memento-vault using its own vault knowledge.
- The benchmark distinguishes agent failure, harness failure, and ambiguous requirements.

acceptance_criteria: Defines 8-12 real issue tasks in a machine-readable fixture
Documents fixture schema and evaluator expectations
Includes category coverage and at least one task requiring vault recall
Provides rubrics that separate agent, harness, and requirement failures
known_risks: Fixture can become stale as GitHub issues evolve
Overfitting the task set to current repo layout
Confusing benchmark metadata with executable Rondo runner behavior

memento_queries: memento-vault Rondo Beislið harness research benchmark task set
checkpoint memento-vault rondo beisli harness research
retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: Recall prior Rondo and Beislið harness research so the benchmark task fixture captures evaluator categories, gates, and failure-mode rubrics.

rubric.success: A clean evaluator can parse the fixture, select representative tasks, and understand expected files, gates, risks, and failure classification without reading the live issue tracker.
rubric.agent_failure: Task metadata is incomplete, categories are missing, or rubrics do not let a reviewer diagnose why an attempted run failed.
rubric.harness_failure: The fixture is valid but the external Rondo runner cannot consume JSON fixtures yet or expects a different adapter contract that was not available when this task was authored.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The benchmark asks the agent to implement future Rondo capabilities rather than preparing static task definitions.

issue.title: [P0] Add GitHub Actions CI for memento-vault gates
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context
This checkout currently has no `.github/` workflow. For agentic/Rondo-style automation, local Beislið gates need a CI mirror so PR readiness is verified outside the agent's mutable session.

## Proposal
Add GitHub Actions CI for memento-vault.

## Initial jobs
- Python lint/format:
  - `ruff check .`
  - `ruff format --check .`
  - `python -m compileall -q memento hooks scripts`
- Test:
  - full `pytest`
  - upload failure logs/artifacts if practical
- MCP/remote focused tests:
  - `tests/test_mcp_server.py`
  - `tests/test_remote_client.py`
  - `tests/test_integration_remote.py`
- Install/register focused tests:
  - `tests/test_install_helpers.py`
  - `tests/test_install_register_mcp.py`
- Sandbox smoke:
  - `scripts/claude_sandbox_smoke.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- CI runs on PRs and pushes to main.
- CI commands mirror local Beislið gates where possible.
- Workflow is documented in README or releasing docs.
- The workflow avoids requiring optional heavy dependencies unless explicitly installed in the job.

acceptance_criteria: CI runs on PRs and pushes to main
CI mirrors local Beislið gates where practical
Optional heavy dependencies are not required by default
Workflow behavior is documented
known_risks: Full pytest may need optional dependencies absent from CI
Duplicating Beislið gates can drift
CI matrix choices can be too slow for agent loops

retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: No vault memory required; use repository CI and Beislið gate documentation only.

rubric.success: A GitHub Actions workflow provides fast safe checks with clear logs and no mandatory optional-heavy setup.
rubric.agent_failure: The workflow omits key local gates, requires unavailable secrets/dependencies, or does not trigger on PR/main events.
rubric.harness_failure: GitHub Actions infrastructure fails independently of repository content, or the evaluator cannot inspect workflow execution logs.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The issue does not specify exact Python versions or whether full pytest must pass without optional benchmark dependencies.

issue.title: [P0] Add release install and package smoke gates
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context
memento-vault has multiple distribution/install surfaces: manual install script, Homebrew formula, Docker/remote deployment, MCP registration, and pi package metadata. Agentic work on this repo needs gates that catch release/install breakage before PR review.

## Proposal
Add release/install/package smoke gates.

## Candidate checks
- `bin/memento-vault --help`
- `python -m memento --help` or safe MCP startup/status smoke
- install script dry-run or temp-HOME smoke
- Homebrew formula syntax/version consistency check
- Docker build or compose config validation where practical
- npm/pi package dry-run once package deps are explicit
- VERSION consistency checks across `VERSION`, formula, package metadata, docs where applicable

## Acceptance criteria
- A lightweight release smoke script exists.
- CI or Beislið can run the safe subset without mutating the developer machine.
- Heavy/optional checks are separated from the fast default path.
- Failures provide actionable output for agents.

expected_touched_areas: scripts or tools release smoke entrypoint
acceptance_criteria: Adds lightweight release/install smoke script
Separates fast safe checks from heavy optional checks
Produces actionable failure output
Can be run by CI or Beislið without mutating the developer machine
known_risks: Install scripts may mutate HOME unless carefully sandboxed
Homebrew/Docker checks can be expensive or host-dependent
Version metadata can drift across package surfaces

retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: No vault memory required; use repository release, install, and packaging surfaces only.

rubric.success: The repo gains a documented fast smoke path that exercises help/version/install metadata and clearly marks heavy checks optional.
rubric.agent_failure: The implementation mutates the real user environment, hides failing subchecks, or does not cover package/install surfaces called out in the issue.
rubric.harness_failure: The host lacks Docker, Homebrew, npm, or other external tools needed only for optional heavy checks.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The issue leaves room to choose which candidate checks are fast defaults versus optional heavy checks.

issue.title: [P0] Add frontmatter schema and docs drift checker
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context
The harness research identified docs/schema drift as a high-value gate. memento-vault's Markdown frontmatter is a source-of-truth interface for retrieval, Obsidian, sync, and agents. If docs drift from what `write_note`, `write_daily_snapshot`, MCP store/capture, and Inception actually write, agents and users get unreliable guidance.

## Proposal
Add a frontmatter/schema drift checker.

## Scope
- Validate `docs/frontmatter-schema.md` against implemented writers and representative fixtures.
- Cover note types/sources emitted by:
  - session triage
  - MCP store/capture
  - daily snapshots
  - Inception pattern notes
  - preserve tool once implemented
- Optionally generate a machine-readable schema or golden examples.

## Acceptance criteria
- A test or script fails when documented frontmatter fields/types/sources drift from implementation.
- Existing docs are updated to match current implementation.
- The checker can be run locally and in CI.

acceptance_criteria: Validates documented frontmatter against representative writers/fixtures
Detects docs drift in CI or local tests
Keeps schema guidance aligned with retrieval/sync/agent behavior
known_risks: Markdown examples may intentionally be illustrative rather than exhaustive
Multiple writers produce different frontmatter subsets
Overly strict tests can block valid schema evolution

retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: No vault memory required; use current frontmatter docs and writer implementations only.

rubric.success: A drift check fails when documented frontmatter diverges from implemented writers while allowing legitimate optional fields.
rubric.agent_failure: The checker only validates static docs text, misses actual writer output, or creates brittle constraints unrelated to stored note behavior.
rubric.harness_failure: A parser dependency or docs extraction step fails in the harness even though the repository change is correct.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The issue does not enumerate every authoritative writer, so the agent may need to document its chosen representative set.

issue.title: [P0] Prevent MCP tool inventory and docs drift
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context
The README/MCP docs have already drifted: the text says one tool count while the code exposes a larger tool surface. Tool drift makes installation docs and agent instructions less trustworthy.

## Proposal
Prevent MCP tool/docs drift by generating tool inventory or testing docs against the registered MCP tools.

## Options
- Generate the MCP tool table from `memento.mcp_server` metadata.
- Add a CI test that fails when README/docs tool names differ from the tool registry.
- Add a small `memento-vault tools --markdown` command used by docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- Current documented tool count/names match implementation.
- Future additions/removals fail tests or update generated docs.
- The fix covers README and any docs/config references that list MCP tools.

acceptance_criteria: Documented MCP tool count and names match implementation
Future additions/removals fail tests or update generated docs
README and docs references are covered
known_risks: MCP server metadata may be hard to inspect without starting external transports
Generated docs can be noisy in diffs
Tool aliases or hidden helper tools may not belong in public docs

retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: No vault memory required; use current MCP server and documentation surfaces only.

rubric.success: A repeatable check or generator keeps public MCP docs synchronized with the registered tool surface.
rubric.agent_failure: The agent updates counts by hand without a future drift guard or validates the wrong tool registry.
rubric.harness_failure: The MCP framework changes runtime metadata shape or fails to import in the clean evaluator environment.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The issue allows either generated docs or a docs-vs-registry test; either is acceptable if documented.

issue.title: [P0] Expand health diagnostics for recall/search failures
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context
Follow-up from #36 (`memento-vault health` / `doctor`). The first health command should ship with cheap, read-only checks. Rich retrieval diagnostics were intentionally deferred to keep the initial PR reviewable.

## Proposal
Expand health diagnostics for recall/search degradation.

## Candidate checks
- Recent recall/search failure rate from retrieval logs.
- Last sanitized/truncated retrieval/search error in `--verbose` / `--json`.
- Distinguish no-results, backend unavailable, backend exception, and low-signal skips.
- Surface likely remediation when search backend is configured but repeatedly failing.

## Constraints
- Default report stays concise.
- No secrets in output.
- Read-only and cheap by default.
- Link behavior back to #36 health report semantics.

acceptance_criteria: Reports recent recall/search failure rate from logs
Surfaces sanitized last errors in verbose or JSON mode
Distinguishes no-results, backend unavailable, backend exception, and low-signal skips
Keeps default health output concise and read-only
known_risks: Retrieval logs can contain sensitive paths or prompt text
Health output must remain cheap and read-only
Different backends may encode failures differently

memento_queries: recall search failures health diagnostics no-results backend unavailable low-signal
retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: Recall prior health-report semantics and retrieval degradation decisions so diagnostics classify no-results, backend failures, and low-signal skips consistently.

rubric.success: Health diagnostics identify degraded recall/search behavior with sanitized, actionable detail in JSON/verbose output.
rubric.agent_failure: The implementation leaks secrets, makes expensive retrieval calls, or collapses distinct failure modes into one vague warning.
rubric.harness_failure: The evaluator has no retrieval log fixture or cannot reproduce local log paths used by the health command.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The exact retrieval log schema is not fully specified, so fixture-backed documented assumptions are acceptable.

issue.title: [P2] Add detail_level include_content and token_budget to memento_search
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context
Memento's MCP `memento_search` includes full note content inline when available. This is convenient, especially for remote notes, but can bloat context. The talk's progressive-disclosure theme suggests returning summaries first and loading full content only when needed.

## Proposal
Add response-shaping parameters to `memento_search`.

## API sketch
- `detail_level: "brief" | "summary" | "full"`
- `include_content: bool`
- `token_budget: int | None`
- `expandable_paths: list[str]` when content is withheld or truncated

## Suggested behavior
- `brief`: path, title, score, maybe note type/certainty.
- `summary`: current compact snippet behavior; no full body by default.
- `full`: include full note content where safe/available.
- If `token_budget` is exceeded, truncate and return expandable paths for `memento_get`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Default search response stays token-efficient.
- Agents can explicitly request full content.
- Results report truncation/expandable paths when budgeted.
- Tests cover all detail levels and budget truncation.

acceptance_criteria: Adds requested memento_search response controls such as detail_level/include_content/token_budget
Preserves safe defaults for existing clients
Tests output shaping and budget behavior
known_risks: Including content can explode token budgets
MCP schema changes can break existing clients
Search backends may return heterogeneous result metadata

retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: No vault memory required; use current MCP search response contract and docs only.

rubric.success: memento_search supports explicit detail/budget controls while existing default behavior remains backward compatible.
rubric.agent_failure: The agent changes retrieval ranking instead of response shaping, breaks MCP schemas, or ignores budget constraints.
rubric.harness_failure: The clean evaluator cannot invoke MCP tools and must rely on unit tests only.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The issue leaves exact parameter names negotiable; compatible documented names are acceptable.

issue.title: Implement Pi SessionEnd-style triage instead of automatic capture queue
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context

The Pi extension currently handles automatic capture by appending summarized lifecycle events to `queue/pi-captures.jsonl` when `piBridge.autoCapture && piBridge.captureQueue` are enabled. Those queued entries are only drained manually via `/memento-flush-queue` / `memento_flush_queue`, which writes each queued summary as a `source: pi` session note.

This is not equivalent to the existing Claude Code end-of-session mining path and can grow indefinitely if enabled.

## How Claude Code is set up today

Claude Code uses native hooks installed by `install.sh`:

- `lib/install_helpers.py::merge_settings` registers `SessionEnd` -> `python3 ~/.claude/hooks/memento-triage.py` with `async: true`, `timeout: 30`.
- `hooks/memento-triage.py` reads Claude hook input from stdin, expects `session_id`, `transcript_path`, and optional `cwd`.
- It parses the transcript through `memento.adapters.parse_transcript()`; today this dispatches to `memento/adapters/claude.py` for Claude JSONL.
- Triage behavior:
  - skip sessions with `<2` exchanges
  - always write a fleeting daily session line and update the project index
  - decide `substantial` via exchange count, edited file count, notable paths, debug keywords, and read-heavy investigation signals
  - run a QMD delta check via `has_new_insight()`
  - for substantial/new sessions, spawn a detached structured-note worker with `--structured-notes`
  - worker sanitizes transcript text, calls `memento.llm.llm_complete()`, parses JSON notes, writes atomic notes via `write_note()`, updates project index, logs triage health
  - auto-commit/reindex after triage; optionally trigger Inception after triage
- Remote/MCP path also has `memento_capture(transcript_path=...)`, but transcript-path mode is stdio/local only and currently only has the Claude transcript adapter implemented.

## Pi details relevant to implementation

Pi extension docs show:

- `agent_end` fires once per user prompt and includes `event.messages` from that prompt.
- `session_shutdown` fires before replacement/exit.
- `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionFile()` returns the persisted Pi session JSONL path.
- `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` returns all session entries.
- Pi sessions are JSONL under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/...`, with message roles/content shapes different from Claude Code (`role: user|assistant|toolResult|bashExecution|custom`, tool calls as `type: "toolCall"`, etc.).

The existing Pi bridge already calls `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionFile()`, but only passes it as metadata/session id for queue entries; `memento.pi_bridge capture` does not support `transcript_path` or full triage.

## Desired behavior

Replace/augment Pi automatic queue capture with a real SessionEnd-style triage path:

1. Add a Pi transcript/session adapter, e.g. `memento/adapters/pi.py`, that parses Pi session JSONL or serialized session entries into the standard `SessionMeta` shape:
   - `cwd`
   - `git_branch`
   - `exchange_count`
   - `user_messages`
   - `files_edited`
   - `files_read`
   - `first_prompt`
   - `last_outcome`
   - `agent: "pi"`
2. Extend `memento.adapters.detect_agent()` / `parse_transcript()` to detect Pi JSONL or accept `agent="pi"`.
3. Expose a bridge command from `memento.pi_bridge` that runs full triage for Pi, preferably by reusing shared triage logic rather than queue flush semantics. Options:
   - refactor common triage from `hooks/memento-triage.py` into importable `memento.triage`, then have both Claude hook and Pi bridge call it; or
   - add a bridge command that invokes the existing triage script with a synthetic hook payload containing `{session_id, transcript_path, cwd}` and `MEMENTO_AGENT=pi`.
4. Update `extensions/memento.ts` so `agent_end`/`session_shutdown` can trigger the full triage path using `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionFile()` instead of appending summaries to `queue/pi-captures.jsonl`.
5. Keep manual queue review as an explicit/manual feature if useful, but do not make automatic capture depend on unbounded queue growth.

## Acceptance criteria

- With Pi `autoCapture` enabled, ending a meaningful Pi session produces the same classes of vault output as Claude Code triage: fleeting line, project session update, and atomic notes only when substantial/new.
- Automatic Pi capture does not append to `queue/pi-captures.jsonl` by default.
- Pi triage is detached/non-blocking enough not to noticeably delay the UI, matching Claude `SessionEnd async` behavior.
- Triage health logging covers Pi failures/successes with enough metadata to debug missing transcript, parse failure, LLM failure, structured-note parse empty, and written notes.
- Add tests for the Pi adapter and bridge path using fixture Pi session JSONL.
- Existing Claude Code triage tests/behavior continue to pass.
- Documentation updates explain the difference between manual queue review and automatic Pi triage.

## Notes / gotchas

- Do not send raw transcript contents to a remote HTTP vault. The current MCP server only allows `transcript_path` in local stdio mode; keep that boundary.
- Reuse existing `sanitize_secrets()` before LLM calls/writes.
- Preserve idempotency/dedup by session id so repeated `agent_end` or `session_shutdown` events do not duplicate notes.
- Consider whether Pi should triage on every `agent_end` or only on `session_shutdown`; Claude triage is session-end scoped, while current Pi `agent_end` fires every prompt and caused queue growth.

acceptance_criteria: Replaces indefinite automatic capture queue behavior with SessionEnd-style triage semantics
Keeps queue/manual review behavior understandable
Adds tests around Pi lifecycle capture and triage parity
known_risks: Large cross-language surface
Risk of losing queued captures
Differences between Pi and Claude lifecycle events
Background workers can hide failures

memento_queries: Pi auto-capture parity Claude triage SessionEnd queued captures
retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: Recall Pi auto-capture parity decisions so SessionEnd queued-capture behavior matches Claude triage semantics without duplicating run evidence.

rubric.success: Pi capture behavior follows the same triage intent as Claude SessionEnd without unbounded opaque queue growth.
rubric.agent_failure: The agent only renames commands, drops captured data, or leaves failures invisible to users.
rubric.harness_failure: The harness cannot simulate Pi lifecycle events or background worker behavior outside the host agent.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The issue is broad; a benchmark evaluator should accept a well-documented first vertical slice if it preserves data and tests parity.

issue.title: Add optional --bare hardened mode for headless Claude workers
issue.body_snapshot:
## Context

Issue #28 fixed the concrete destructive-action path by sandboxing headless Claude workers with:

- `--tools ""`
- `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config "{}"`
- `--permission-mode default`
- `--disallowedTools ...` as defense in depth

That blocks built-in tools, inherited MCP servers, and the observed `git push` / `gh pr create` failure mode.

## Follow-up

Consider an optional hardened mode that also adds `--bare` for headless Claude calls.

Claude Code documents `--bare` as skipping hooks, LSP, plugin sync, attribution, auto-memory, background prefetches, keychain reads, and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery. That would further reduce lifecycle/config inheritance for detached SessionEnd workers.

## Trade-off

`--bare` changes auth behavior: Anthropic auth is strictly `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `apiKeyHelper` via `--settings`. It may break users relying on normal Claude Code subscription/keychain login.

Suggested shape:

- Keep the current sandbox as the compatible default.
- Add an opt-in config flag for hardened mode, e.g. `claude_bare_headless: true`.
- Document that hardened mode requires API-key or apiKeyHelper auth.
- Add command-construction tests for the opt-in path.

acceptance_criteria: Adds optional hardened bare/headless mode
Avoids unsafe interactive assumptions for worker agents
Documents configuration and tradeoffs
Keeps existing default behavior unchanged
known_risks: Security hardening can accidentally remove useful context
Headless worker environments differ by host
Environment variables and subprocess output may leak sensitive data

retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: No vault memory required; use current hook and wrapper behavior only.

rubric.success: Headless workers can opt into stricter non-interactive behavior without regressing normal interactive sessions.
rubric.agent_failure: The implementation makes hardened behavior the default, leaks hidden context, or does not test worker-safe paths.
rubric.harness_failure: The harness cannot model the exact headless Claude worker environment described by the issue.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The issue leaves the flag name and exact disabled features flexible if the chosen semantics are documented.

issue.title: Pi auto-capture parity with Claude triage
issue.body_snapshot:
## Problem

Pi support currently provides lifecycle retrieval tools and manual/queued capture, but it does not have parity with Claude's SessionEnd triage behavior. Auto-capture is disabled by default in the Pi extension, and when enabled it queues a short candidate summary rather than running the full structured note extraction pipeline.

## Current state

- Claude uses SessionEnd hooks to parse transcripts, score substantiality, write fleeting/project summaries, and run structured note extraction.
- Pi bridge exposes manual `memento_capture` and queue tools.
- Pi bridge has `autoCapture: false` by default.
- Pi lifecycle auto-capture, when enabled, queues summarized candidate captures from lifecycle events instead of triaging the full session transcript.

## Desired state

Define and ship intentional Pi auto-capture behavior with clear parity boundaries:

- Opt-in or default behavior is explicit and documented.
- Pi session capture can preserve durable session knowledge without relying on manual `/memento` use.
- Capture behavior is safe, reviewable, and does not surprise users with unapproved writes.
- The implementation either reaches Claude triage parity or clearly documents why queued summaries remain the supported Pi model.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide whether Pi auto-capture should be default-off queued capture, default-on queue, or full structured extraction.
- Document Pi capture lifecycle events and user-facing configuration.
- Add tests covering the selected behavior.
- Add status/diagnostics that make it obvious whether Pi capture is enabled and whether it queued/wrote anything.
- Avoid coupling Pi to Claude-only transcript formats.

## Out of scope

This issue does not cover the immediate Claude SessionEnd hotfix for invalid headless MCP config, binary lookup, or triage failure observability.

acceptance_criteria: Narrows Pi auto-capture behavior toward Claude triage parity
Preserves provenance/source metadata
Tests capture routing and queue/triage outcomes
known_risks: Subtle source/provenance mismatches
Potential duplicate captures
Queue processing and triage may have different failure semantics

memento_queries: Pi auto-capture parity with Claude triage provenance source pi session note
retrieval_context.expected_query_intent: Recall Pi and Claude triage provenance decisions so source, session, and note metadata remain comparable across agents.

rubric.success: Pi and Claude capture paths have documented, tested parity for durable knowledge extraction semantics.
rubric.agent_failure: The agent implements a parallel incompatible path or loses metadata needed to distinguish Pi captures.
rubric.harness_failure: Host-specific Pi extension hooks are unavailable in the evaluator and require unit-test simulation.
rubric.ambiguous_requirements: The phrase parity can mean exact implementation reuse or equivalent behavior; either is acceptable when tested and documented.
